> Yes but what can you achieve with this?

I think I'm not explaining myself. Will start from the beginnig: 

In consul, they have a feature called connect, that works like as a service-mesh. Services communicate peer to peer in mTLS by using proxies. These usualy are deployed as sidecar, so the application exposes the service port locally in a internal network namespace and the proxy exposes externally the service but in TLS and verifying the connections.

Beside this, you can configure the proxy to also expose a path of the service in plain HTTP, to be used as a healthcheck or metrics endpoint. This is an example configuration of a service in consul:

```
  {
    "ID": "05b80bcb-26e1-8d84-a15c-e8029f28ea65",
    "Node": "node1",
    "Address": "10.171.0.33",
    "Datacenter": "dc1",
    "TaggedAddresses": {
      "lan": "10.171.0.33",
      "lan_ipv4": "10.171.0.33",
      "wan": "10.171.0.33",
      "wan_ipv4": "10.171.0.33"
    },
    "NodeMeta": {},
    "ServiceKind": "",
    "ServiceID": "count-api-9001",
    "ServiceName": "count-api",
    "ServiceTags": [
      "demo",
      "meigas"
    ],
    "ServiceAddress": "10.171.0.33",
    "ServiceTaggedAddresses": {
      "lan_ipv4": {
        "Address": "10.171.0.33",
        "Port": 9001
      },
      "wan_ipv4": {
        "Address": "10.171.0.33",
        "Port": 9001
      }
    },
    "ServiceWeights": {
      "Passing": 1,
      "Warning": 1
    },
    "ServiceMeta": {},
    "ServicePort": 9001,
    "ServiceEnableTagOverride": false,
    "ServiceProxy": {
      "MeshGateway": {},
      "Expose": {}
    },
    "ServiceConnect": {},
    "CreateIndex": 1209594065,
    "ModifyIndex": 1209594065
  }
```

And the proxy configuration for that service:

```
  {
    "ID": "05b80bcb-26e1-8d84-a15c-e8029f28ea65",
    "Node": "node1",
    "Address": "10.171.0.33",
    "Datacenter": "dc1",
    "TaggedAddresses": {
      "lan": "10.171.0.33",
      "lan_ipv4": "10.171.0.33",
      "wan": "10.171.0.33",
      "wan_ipv4": "10.171.0.33"
    },
    "NodeMeta": {},
    "ServiceKind": "connect-proxy",
    "ServiceID": "count-api-9001-sidecar-proxy",
    "ServiceName": "count-api-sidecar-proxy",
    "ServiceTags": [],
    "ServiceAddress": "10.171.0.33",
    "ServiceTaggedAddresses": {
      "lan_ipv4": {
        "Address": "10.171.0.33",
        "Port": 29149
      },
      "wan_ipv4": {
        "Address": "10.171.0.33",
        "Port": 29149
      }
    },
    "ServiceWeights": {
      "Passing": 1,
      "Warning": 1
    },
    "ServiceMeta": {},
    "ServicePort": 29149,
    "ServiceEnableTagOverride": false,
    "ServiceProxy": {
      "DestinationServiceName": "count-api",
      "DestinationServiceID": "count-api-9001",
      "LocalServiceAddress": "127.0.0.1",
      "LocalServicePort": 9001,
      "Config": {
        "bind_address": "0.0.0.0",
        "bind_port": 29149,
        "protocol": "http"
      },
      "MeshGateway": {
        "Mode": "local"
      },
      "Expose": {
        "Paths": [
          {
            "ListenerPort": 21107,
            "Path": "/health",
            "LocalPathPort": 9001,
            "Protocol": "http",
            "ParsedFromCheck": false
          },
          {
            "ListenerPort": 21228,
            "Path": "/metrics",
            "LocalPathPort": 9001,
            "Protocol": "http",
            "ParsedFromCheck": false
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    "ServiceConnect": {},
    "CreateIndex": 1209594068,
    "ModifyIndex": 1209594068
  }
```

The service is exposing the port 9001, but only locally in the network namespace and only reachable directly by the proxy.
Using this configuration the proxy would expose 3 ports to be consumed:

- port 29149: mTLS port for the proxied service to be consumed (discovered as `__meta_consul_service_port`)
- port 21107: /health endpoint of the proxied service (HTTP exposed externally)
- port 21228: /metrics endpoint of the proxied service (HTTP exposed externally)

Right now, as the the consul discovery exists in prometheus, there's no way of obtaining that /metrics address:port to request aplication metrics if that application is inside the service mesh.

As I see it (maybe I'm wrong) there're two ways of solving this. One is by simple adding new `__meta` labels. As the exposed paths is a list of path/port, and the meta could colide, we need to set something in the label name to differentiate them.

```
__meta_consul_proxy_expoxed_path_port_health = 21107
__meta_consul_proxy_expoxed_path_local_port_health = 9001
__meta_consul_proxy_expoxed_path_port_metrics = 21228
__meta_consul_proxy_expoxed_path_local_port_metrics = 9001
```

That way I could use __relabel_config__ to change the `__address__` by using the port defined in `__meta_consul_proxy_expoxed_path_port_metrics` 

Another option would be to add a new target per each of the exposed paths defined. Something like:


```
target1:
(common __meta)
__meta_consul_proxy_expoxed_paths_path = /health
__meta_consul_proxy_expoxed_paths_port = 21107
__meta_consul_proxy_expoxed_paths_local_port = 9001

target2:
(common __meta)
__meta_consul_proxy_expoxed_paths_path = /metrics
__meta_consul_proxy_expoxed_paths_port = 21228
__meta_consul_proxy_expoxed_paths_local_port = 9001
```
That way we could also filter on the  `__meta_consul_proxy_expoxed_paths_path` and use the `__meta_consul_proxy_expoxed_paths_port` in the `__address__` to get the metrics.

What do you think? I'm not an expert in prometheus (started using it a few months ago) so maybe there're a lot of things I'm missing. In any case, let me know how do you think this should be implemented. Thanks!

issue_context.title: Add consul exposed sidecar ports
issue_context.body:
## Proposal
Add consul exposed ports using sidecars to the target labels.

Consul has the ability to expose paths for aplications making the service port only accesible internally but some application paths could be consumed externally (as /metrics for example). This can be seen in the consul documentation: https://www.consul.io/docs/connect/registration/service-registration#expose-paths-configuration-reference

This would allow us to deploy applications with the consul connect sidecar, but expose the metrics to be consumed by prometheus externally.

Regarding implementation details. On the consul discovery if the service is a proxy exposed paths could be iterated and returned as labels (for example `__meta_consul_exposed_path_<path>_port: listener_port`)
